author: Nicole Wilson
title: Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) is Strs Ohio’s Largest Position
text:
Posted by Nicole Wilson on May 3rd, 2018 // No Comments
Strs Ohio decreased its position in shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 4.3% during the 4th quarter, according to the company in its most recent disclosure with the SEC. The fund owned 4,220,194 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 187,834 shares during the quarter. Apple makes up about 3.1% of Strs Ohio’s holdings, making the stock its largest position. Strs Ohio owned 0.08% of Apple worth $714,183,000 at the end of the most recent reporting period.
Other hedge funds have also recently modified their holdings of the company. Capital Insight Partners LLC lifted its position in shares of Apple by 4.9% during the 4th quarter. Capital Insight Partners LLC now owns 6,292 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $1,065,000 after acquiring an additional 293 shares during the period. Corundum Group Inc. lifted its position in shares of Apple by 15.4% during the 3rd quarter. Corundum Group Inc. now owns 2,242 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $346,000 after acquiring an additional 299 shares during the period. Crossvault Capital Management LLC lifted its position in shares of Apple by 0.5% during the 3rd quarter. Crossvault Capital Management LLC now owns 65,678 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $10,122,000 after acquiring an additional 300 shares during the period. Welch Investments LLC lifted its position in shares of Apple by 18.7% during the 3rd quarter. Welch Investments LLC now owns 1,907 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $294,000 after acquiring an additional 300 shares during the period. Finally, Nadler Financial Group Inc. raised its position in shares of Apple by 0.5% during the 4th quarter. Nadler Financial Group Inc. now owns 57,894 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $9,797,000 after purchasing an additional 305 shares during the last quarter. 61.18% of the stock is currently owned by institutional investors. Shares of NASDAQ AAPL opened at $176.57 on Thursday. Apple has a 1-year low of $142.20 and a 1-year high of $183.50. The company has a quick ratio of 1.20, a current ratio of 1.24 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74. The stock has a market capitalization of $838,531.38, a price-to-earnings ratio of 19.17, a P/E/G ratio of 1.26 and a beta of 1.26.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last issued its quarterly earnings results on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 EPS for the quarter, topping the consensus estimate of $2.69 by $0.04. Apple had a net margin of 21.13% and a return on equity of 37.37%. The company had revenue of $61.14 billion during the quarter, compared to analysts’ expectations of $60.94 billion. During the same quarter in the previous year, the company earned $2.10 EPS. Apple’s revenue was up 15.6% on a year-over-year basis. equities research analysts anticipate that Apple will post 11.3 earnings per share for the current year.
The company also recently disclosed a quarterly dividend, which will be paid on Thursday, May 17th. Investors of record on Monday, May 14th will be issued a dividend of $0.73 per share. The ex-dividend date is Friday, May 11th. This represents a $2.92 dividend on an annualized basis and a yield of 1.65%. This is a boost from Apple’s previous quarterly dividend of $0.63. Apple’s payout ratio is currently 27.36%.
Apple announced that its Board of Directors has approved a share buyback program on Tuesday, May 1st that allows the company to repurchase $100.00 billion in outstanding shares. This repurchase authorization allows the iPhone maker to reacquire up to 11.9% of its shares through open market purchases. Shares repurchase programs are usually an indication that the company’s leadership believes its stock is undervalued.
Several research analysts recently issued reports on AAPL shares. Zacks Investment Research upgraded Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $190.00 price objective for the company in a research report on Wednesday, January 3rd. Rosenblatt Securities reiterated a “buy” rating and issued a $180.00 price target on shares of Apple in a report on Friday, January 19th. UBS set a $190.00 price target on Apple and gave the company a “buy” rating in a report on Friday, January 5th. Maxim Group boosted their price objective on shares of Apple from $193.00 to $204.00 and gave the company a “buy” rating in a research note on Friday, January 12th. Finally, Morgan Stanley reissued a “buy” rating and set a $205.00 price objective (up from $200.00) on shares of Apple in a research note on Tuesday, January 23rd. Two analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, sixteen have given a hold rating, thirty-three have given a buy rating and two have issued a strong buy rating to the company. Apple presently has a consensus rating of “Buy” and a consensus price target of $203.58.

The shares were sold at an average price of $166.42, for a total transaction of $11,564,692.22. The sale was disclosed in a legal filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is accessible through this link . Also, insider Luca Maestri sold 39,122 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Friday, April 13th. The shares were sold at an average price of $174.66, for a total transaction of $6,833,048.52. Following the transaction, the insider now owns 64,475 shares of the company’s stock, valued at approximately $11,261,203.50. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . In the last 90 days, insiders have sold 125,988 shares of company stock valued at $21,336,201. Corporate insiders own 0.06% of the company’s stock.
